correctness.rationale: For every connected matching-deleted clique G the incidence operator B has image the coordinate-sum-zero subspace and transpose kernel the constant vectors. Characteristic-two BB^T restricts to a swap involution for odd n and square-zero matched-pair blocks for even n; their ranks give both complete Jordan decompositions. The periodic and attraction-basin formulas follow from the resulting kernels and equal-sized linear fibers. Independently constructed GF(2) matrices matched all ranks for n=3..16 (77 graph parameter instances), and direct vertex-edge evolution matched all enumerated 3,995,516 binary initial states for n=3..7 (16 instances). The unbounded conclusion follows from the proof, not the tests.

value.rationale: A graph family defined by a natural matching perturbation of a clique admits a full parameter-uniform Jordan and attraction census. Parity of the underlying clique switches all recurrent behavior: odd order has an exact two-cycle probability 1-q^{-k}, while even order has global nilpotence. The perfect-matching rank discontinuity at orders divisible by four identifies a concrete structural boundary invisible to real adjacency ranks. This exact phase diagram is motivated by topology-dependence of XOR dynamics, not a pointwise numerical artifact.
